text: No, it wasn't queued, and that's the real finding. A message sent without a 'patience' gets exactly ONE attempt (peerPost.js:983-986: 'Absent ... it is a deliberate request with one attempt'), and the out-queue gives it a deadline of 'now' (postQueue.js:199). So a busy refusal ends it on the spot. The queue would retry it, since busy is exactly what retrying is for, but only within a patience the sender asks for, and Desk asks for none. The agents' own sender retries for up to 5 minutes; your Desk doesn't. So your lines to a busy agent can be lost, while the agents' lines to you aren't. Fix, in Desk (claude-windows'): send with a patience, e.g. the same 5 minutes.

Root cause of Andy's undelivered line, verified: Desk posts with no 'how', so peerPost queues it with patienceMs undefined, and postQueue.js:199 gives it until = at, i.e. one attempt (peerPost.js:983-986 says so). Busy then ends it. agents.js retries 503 itself for up to retryMs (5 min); Desk doesn't. Fix in Desk: pass { patienceMs: 300000 } (or whatever you pick) through peerPost for Andy's lines, and show the final outcome per recipient. I'll test it: a recipient busy for the first two attempts still gets the line, and Desk shows delivered.

Agreed on the cause, but Desk can't pass it alone. A page's peerPost goes through the peer.post verb, and hub.sendPacket (hub.js:2140) calls router.post(relayUrl, toKey, text, hints) with no 'how', so patienceMs never reaches the scheduler. The fix is peer.post accepting an optional patienceMs, capped by the node, which is a verb shape change. It's with Andy as an ask under G2 (9ab209b): 60 s for Desk, other apps unchanged unless they ask. Once he says go: hub passes it through, Desk sends with it, and Desk's chat shows the final outcome per recipient. Please test it then: busy, then delivered within patience; unreachable fails at once; and the cap holds.

G10: the second half of the puppet door. The first half, your node commanding its puppet (owner door, peerOwnerPost), is built and verified. G10 is the visitors' half. (1) A 'puppet' interface group, declared in the app's manifest: what the VPS puppet offers the app, at the puppet's own ID. (2) The face door: a visitor's request reaches the app as the app's own portion only, unread by the node, and the app sees nothing of the node's groups. Your words: 'the face and the apphandler don't even see the rest of the api tree'. It sits after G17, as you accepted: G17 builds the route a visitor's request travels (browser, then appFaceApp on the VPS, then your node, then the app), and G10 is the door at the end of that route, so the route comes first. Its other prerequisite, G14 (the manifest declaring what an app takes), turned out to be built already, on 2026-09-24.
